title: Reconstruct Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: Separate rationale prompting from answer aggregation, then implement self-consistency voting with uniform and weighted samples.

parts.title: Why intermediate steps help
parts.prompt: How can a rationale improve a frozen model without changing its weights?
parts.answer: Intermediate text gives the model extra computational tokens and conditions later predictions on partial results. It also demonstrates the desired decomposition pattern in-context.
hints: The scratchpad becomes part of the sequence.

parts.title: Why scale matters
parts.prompt: Why did chain-of-thought gains emerge mainly in sufficiently large models?
parts.answer: The prompt can elicit only capabilities represented by the model. Larger models more reliably execute multi-step patterns; smaller models often imitate the format without maintaining correct state.
hints: Prompting reveals rather than installs a capability.
Format accuracy is not reasoning accuracy.

parts.title: Self-consistency
parts.prompt: Why can sampling several reasoning paths and voting outperform greedy decoding?
parts.answer: A correct answer may be reachable through many valid paths, while individual mistakes are diverse. Marginalizing approximately by vote reinforces answers supported across independent trajectories.
hints: Voting operates on final answers, not rationale text.

parts.title: Implement self-consistency voting
parts.prompt: Return the most frequent numeric answer; break ties by the smallest answer.

parts.title: Implement weighted voting
parts.prompt: Sum sample weights by numeric answer and return the highest-weight answer, breaking ties by the smallest answer.
